```plato

    //==
    // # Integration
    //
    // SEMI-IMPLICIT (SYMPLECTIC) EULER, and the choice matters more than its two
    // lines suggest: velocity is advanced by the acceleration FIRST, and position
    // is then advanced by the NEW velocity.
    //
    //     v' = v + a dt          then          x' = x + v' dt
    //
    // Explicit Euler uses the OLD velocity for the position update. On the orbit
    // and the spring — the two motions a rigid-body engine spends its life
    // integrating — explicit Euler gains energy every step and the motion spirals
    // outward without bound, at any step size. Semi-implicit Euler is symplectic:
    // its energy error is bounded and oscillates rather than accumulating, so a
    // pendulum swings forever at very nearly the right amplitude instead of
    // winding up. It costs exactly the same arithmetic. There is no case for
    // explicit Euler in this library.
    //
    // Higher order was also rejected, for a different reason: velocity-Verlet and
    // RK4 both want to evaluate forces more than once per step, and a step that
    // contains a CONTACT SOLVE has no smooth force field to re-evaluate. The
    // accuracy those methods buy is spent on the smooth part of a simulation whose
    // error is dominated by the non-smooth part.
    //
    // Orientation is advanced by the quaternion rate q' = q + (omega (x) q) dt / 2
    // and renormalized. That is first order in the same sense, and the
    // renormalization is what keeps repeated products on the unit sphere.
    // (https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Semi-implicit_Euler_method)

    // The orientation after spinning at `angular` radians per second for
    // `seconds`, renormalized. The quaternion rate is half the angular velocity,
    // as a pure quaternion, multiplied onto the current orientation from the left.
    IntegrateOrientation(orientation: Quaternion, angular: Vector3D, seconds: Number): Quaternion
        => (orientation
            + Quaternion(angular.X, angular.Y, angular.Z, 0.0) * orientation * (0.5 * seconds))
            .Normalize;
```
